items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: I don't want it to sound like Mozart or Beethoven.

ctx.x: Well, truthfully, Bach was quite a guy, there's no question about it. But I liked him for what he did, and I liked some of the others. Like you say, Mozart, Chopin, a lot of those guys for what they did. Because everybody had a story to tell, and it reflected in there what they were doing. In their works, and that was the outlook that I had upon it. In other words, say, for instance, if I'm going to
play Bach, I don't want it to sound like Mozart or Beethoven. I want to know that I'm playing Bach.

So I had respect for all of them. But, really, I never did put myself -- have any preference. It was just a matter that there were certain things that I wanted to do musically, and I wanted to get that done.
